In addition to a concern for humans and their social structures, his early training in science led to a comparable concern for the natural world and animal communication, as well as information and learning theory across these contexts. Among the major concepts generally associated with his name are framing, metacommunication, cybernetics, double bind, feedback, schismogenesis, abduction, difference, deutero-learning, mind, natural history, context, and pattern. These are most adequately understood as a system of ideas rather than discrete units since Bateson viewed knowledge as integrated. References and Further Readings     * Bateson, G. ( 1936 ). Naven .
